cases.sentence: وصلت الطالبة التي تحدثت معها أمس.

derivationStages.stageRecord: On this reading, وصلت is the feminine singular arrival verb, and الطالبة is its Theme subject, initially in Spec-VP. The definite article is retained within the whole-word nominal terminal; it is not represented as a separate morpheme. The relative predicate تحدثت has a silent subject and an interlocutor phrase معها. Its silent subject can be first-person singular, second-person singular, or third-person feminine singular, since the unvocalized verb does not distinguish these possibilities. These feature alternatives do not change the structure. The relational head مع takes the feminine pronominal complement ها, assigning it genitive Case; their clitic realization supplies the single input word معها. The temporal nominal أمس remains separate until its attachment is determined.
derivationStages.statement: Construct an intransitive arrival predicate and a relative predicate with an oblique resumptive pronoun.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Each verb raises from its previously represented V position to finite I, leaving a silent head trace. Subjects remain in Spec-VP; finite I licenses their nominative Case and the relative pro, producing the Arabic verb-before-subject order without moving the overt subject. Yesterday adjoins to the relative V′, so it dates the conversation rather than the arrival. The relative CP contains التي in C and a silent operator in Spec-CP. This is a base-generated resumptive dependency, not movement out of the pronominal complement: the operator binds ها, and the relative CP adjoins to the student's N′. The student is therefore the person spoken with. The relative subject must be distinct from the locally bound feminine pronoun under Principle B. The completed pronunciation is وصلت الطالبة التي تحدثت معها أمس.
